ramsey.RAction.edge_clique_profiles(state: RSearchState) → ndarray[Any, dtype[uint16]][source]

Count affected cliques by current color-one edge count.

profiles[e, k] is the number of indexed cliques containing edge e that currently have exactly k color-one edges.

RSearchState constructs this information lazily and maintains it incrementally after each edge flip. Return an owned copy so this function retains its original value-returning behavior.

ramsey.RActionFlexibility.calculate_action_flexibility_landscape(state: RSearchState, analysis: RActionAnalysis | None = None, budgets: Iterable[int] = (0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20), *, candidate_mask: ndarray[Any, dtype[bool]] | None = None) → RActionFlexibilityLandscape[source]

Calculate the exact future flexibility produced by candidate flips.

The source state is never mutated. A private scratch state reuses the incremental action-profile machinery, making exact counterfactuals much cheaper than rebuilding K5 incidence information for every candidate.

Pareto dominance maximizes exact score reward and every resulting F(b) component simultaneously. No arbitrary scalar weighting is introduced.

ramsey.RActionLandscape module

Directional structure surrounding every single-edge flip.

class ramsey.RActionLandscape.RActionLandscape(source_state: RSearchState, state_version: int, analysis: RActionAnalysis, red_profiles: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint16]], blue_profiles: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint16]], red_deficit_deltas: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]], blue_deficit_deltas: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]], red_violations_destroyed: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]], red_violations_created: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]], blue_violations_destroyed: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]], blue_violations_created: ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]])[source]

Bases: object

Preserve the information hidden by a scalar edge-flip reward.

Rows correspond to host-graph edges. Deficit columns run from zero (already monochromatic) through edges_per_clique.

red_profiles[e, d] counts K5s containing edge e that are currently d edge recolorings away from all red. The blue profile has the same meaning in the opposite color direction.

The delta arrays describe the exact global change to those two distributions if the corresponding edge is flipped.

class ramsey.RArchive.RSQLiteArchive(database_path: str | Path)[source]

Bases: RArchive

SQLite archive compatible with the original coloring database.

Binary colorings are packed into bits. A K43 coloring therefore occupies 113 bytes rather than 903 bytes.

best_colorings(limit: int = 10, graph: RGraph | None = None) → list[RArchiveRecord][source]

Save or observe one exact coloring.

The histogram and score are calculated from the coloring inside the archive boundary. Callers cannot accidentally supply metadata belonging to a different coloring.

If the coloring already exists, its observation count and most recent provenance are updated.

ramsey.RConstructionArchiveQueue module

Live cyclic queue construction backed by a Ramsey archive.

class ramsey.RConstructionArchiveQueue.RArchiveQueueConstruction(archive: RArchive, rng: Generator, minimum_score: int | None = None, maximum_score: int | None = None, limit: int | None = None)[source]

Bases: RConstruction

Consume repeated, refreshed archive queues without replacement.

One queue generation is frozen and shuffled, then every seed in it is consumed exactly once. After it is exhausted, the archive is queried again. Results archived during one generation can therefore become seeds in the next generation without changing the population halfway through the current generation.

If limit is supplied, the archive query first selects the best limit eligible records by its normal score ordering and this construction then shuffles that active pool.

ramsey.RConstructionEdgeRisk module

Incremental edge construction guided by partial-K5 future risk.

class ramsey.RConstructionEdgeRisk.REdgeRiskConstruction(rng: Generator, minimum_pressure_edges: int = 4, risk_epsilon: float = 1e-12, observer: Callable[[REdgeRiskConstructionProgress], None] | None = None)[source]

Bases: RConstruction

Color K43 one edge at a time while minimizing partial-K5 risk.

Edges are processed in one random order. Step parity proposes the globally balanced red/blue alternating color. If the partial K5s containing the current edge give one candidate color strictly less expected future monochromatic risk, that color overrides the alternating proposal.

A partial K5 contributes risk only after at least minimum_pressure_edges edges of one color have been assigned while none of the opposite color have been assigned.

ramsey.RConstructionExoo module

Published Exoo zero-score construction for the R(5,5) K42 graph.

class ramsey.RConstructionExoo.RConstructionExoo[source]

Bases: RConstruction

Construct Exoo’s published zero-score red/blue coloring of K42.

The construction follows Exoo(42) as restated and proved in:

Ge, Jayasooriya, Qiu, Sun, Yuan (2023), “Study of Exoo’s Lower Bound for Ramsey number R(5,5)”, arXiv:2212.12630, Definition 1.2.

It begins with the published Cyclic(43) distance coloring, deletes vertex 0, and changes sixteen specified red edges to blue.

RGraph labels the resulting K42 vertices 0..41. Internally this class maps them to Exoo’s surviving labels 1..42 while constructing the coloring, then returns the ordinary canonical RColoring.

ramsey.RConstructionK5Risk module

Incremental K5 construction guided by overlapping partial-K5 risk.

class ramsey.RConstructionK5Risk.RK5RiskConstruction(rng: Generator, minimum_pressure_edges: int = 4, preferred_new_edges: int = 4, risk_epsilon: float = 1e-12)[source]

Bases: RConstruction

Build a coloring by completing carefully selected K5s.

The constructor prefers incomplete K5s having at least preferred_new_edges uncolored edges, while choosing the most constrained member of that group. With the default value four, the construction naturally grows from one completed K5 into K5s sharing four vertices with already colored structure.

Whenever the existing assignments are compatible with one of the 12 balanced C5/complement-C5 K5 colorings, only those patterns are considered. Otherwise all compatible nonmonochromatic assignments of the target K5’s remaining edges are considered.

Each candidate is scored jointly over every partial K5 containing at least one newly colored edge. Lower expected future monochromatic risk wins.

ramsey.REdgeFlipability.calculate_edge_flipability(state: RSearchState, analysis: RActionAnalysis | None = None) → REdgeFlipabilityAnalysis[source]

Calculate the structural flipability of every host-graph edge.

For one K5 containing edge e, let k be the number of K5 edges having e’s current color. The discrete local flipability is

k - 1.

This is literally the number of same-color edges that remain in the K5 if e is flipped. A unique minority-color edge therefore has local flipability zero, while an edge in a monochromatic K5 has local flipability nine.

Global edge flipability is the integer sum of those local values. Every edge of the same complete host graph participates in the same number of K5s, so the totals are directly comparable without an arbitrary continuous weighting.

ramsey.REnvironment module

Validation and application of state transitions.

class ramsey.REnvironment.REnvironment(graph: RGraph, objective: RObjective, memory: RMemory, config: REnvironmentConfig | None = None)[source]

Bases: object

Own one Ramsey-search episode without choosing actions.

The environment:

  • owns the mutable search state;

  • asks memory which actions are blocked;

  • applies aspiration and deadlock fallback;

  • validates and applies selected edge flips;

  • tracks the best exact score and coloring;

  • determines episode termination and truncation.

It deliberately does not select an action. A greedy search, neural policy, evolutionary algorithm, or other search strategy must select from the environment’s available actions.

analyze_actions(use_cache: bool = True) → REnvironmentAnalysis[source]

Calculate exact consequences and availability for all actions.

available_action_mask_fast(use_cache: bool = True) → ndarray[Any, dtype[bool]][source]

Return availability without full all-action analysis.

Exact score rewards are calculated only for blocked edges when aspiration must be evaluated. If every action is blocked, exact score rewards are calculated for all edges to provide the deadlock fallback.

ramsey.RFlexibility.calculate_flexibility(rewards: ndarray[Any, dtype[integer]], budgets: Iterable[int] = (0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20), *, action_mask: ndarray[Any, dtype[bool]] | None = None) → RFlexibilityProfile[source]

Calculate the local flexibility curve from exact action rewards.

F(b) is the fraction of considered actions whose exact score reward is at least -b. Thus F(0) counts improving and neutral actions; F(5) additionally permits actions that temporarily worsen the score by at most five.

action_mask can restrict the measurement to actions available to a particular search mechanism. Omit it to measure the structural flexibility of the complete action space.

ramsey.RK5Action.analyze_k5_patterns(state: RSearchState, target_clique: int) → RK5PatternAnalysis[source]

Evaluate every nonmonochromatic recoloring of one bad K5 exactly.

Neighboring K5s are aggregated by two sufficient statistics:

  • which subset of the target’s ten edges they share; and

  • how many blue edges they have outside the target.

A K5 can share only a K2, K3, K4, or K5 with the target, so only a small number of shared-edge masks actually occur. This reduces the 1,022-pattern calculation from tens of millions of clique-by-pattern operations to a small grouped table without losing information.

class ramsey.RSearch.RSearch(environment: REnvironment, policy: RPolicy)[source]

Bases: object

Run an environment using one interchangeable policy.

RSearch coordinates an episode but does not:

  • construct seed colorings;

  • choose how action rewards are calculated;

  • implement tabu memory;

  • persist results;

  • plot results; or

  • train neural networks.

Those responsibilities belong to separate components.

    If false, only summary information and important coloring snapshots are retained.

ramsey.RState module

Mutable incremental state for one active search attempt.

class ramsey.RState.RSearchState(coloring: RColoring)[source]

Bases: object

Incrementally maintained state for symmetric two-color search.

RSearchState is the sole owner of mutable coloring, clique-count, histogram, and score data.

property action_profiles: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint16]]

Return incrementally maintained all-edge clique profiles.

profiles[e, k] is the number of indexed cliques containing edge e that currently contain exactly k color-one edges.

The profiles are constructed only on first use. Once they exist, every edge flip updates only the profile contributions of cliques affected by that flip.

apply_edge_flip(edge: int) → int[source]

Flip one edge and return the exact score reduction.

A positive result means the score improved. A negative result means the score became worse.

apply_edge_recoloring(edges: ndarray[Any, dtype[integer]], colors: ndarray[Any, dtype[integer]]) → int[source]

Recolor several distinct edges and return exact score reduction.

Only edges whose requested color differs from the current color are mutated.

Each changed edge goes through apply_edge_flip(), preserving all incrementally maintained state:

  • edge colors

  • K5 color counts

  • histogram

  • monochromatic score

  • action-profile cache

  • state version

property clique_size: int

Return the forbidden clique size maintained by this state.

property color_one_counts: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint8]]

Return a read-only view of per-clique color-one counts.

property colors: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint8]]

Return a read-only view of the current edge colors.

copy() → RSearchState[source]

Return an independent state with the same current coloring.

The copied state begins at version zero because it has its own independent mutation history.

Analyze two simultaneous edge flips without mutating the supplied state.

Clique changes are measured from the original state directly to the final state. Intermediate events caused by only the first flip are intentionally excluded, so the returned event decomposition is the exact net causal footprint of the pair.

ramsey.RVertexBalanceAction.analyze_vertex_balance_transfers(state: RSearchState) → RVertexBalanceAnalysis[source]

Analyze every pivot transfer that moves both endpoint imbalances toward zero.

For donor u, recipient v, and pivot w the required colors are:

u-w = blue (1) v-w = red (0)

Recoloring those edges to red and blue transfers one unit of blue degree from u to v while leaving w and the global blue-edge count unchanged.

class ramsey.REnvironment(graph: RGraph, objective: RObjective, memory: RMemory, config: REnvironmentConfig | None = None)[source]

Bases: object

Own one Ramsey-search episode without choosing actions.

The environment:

  • owns the mutable search state;

  • asks memory which actions are blocked;

  • applies aspiration and deadlock fallback;

  • validates and applies selected edge flips;

  • tracks the best exact score and coloring;

  • determines episode termination and truncation.

It deliberately does not select an action. A greedy search, neural policy, evolutionary algorithm, or other search strategy must select from the environment’s available actions.

analyze_actions(use_cache: bool = True) → REnvironmentAnalysis[source]

Calculate exact consequences and availability for all actions.

available_action_mask_fast(use_cache: bool = True) → ndarray[Any, dtype[bool]][source]

Return availability without full all-action analysis.

Exact score rewards are calculated only for blocked edges when aspiration must be evaluated. If every action is blocked, exact score rewards are calculated for all edges to provide the deadlock fallback.

available_actions() → ndarray[Any, dtype[int32]][source]

Return the indexes of currently available edge actions.

class ramsey.RSQLiteArchive(database_path: str | Path)[source]

Bases: RArchive

SQLite archive compatible with the original coloring database.

Binary colorings are packed into bits. A K43 coloring therefore occupies 113 bytes rather than 903 bytes.

best_colorings(limit: int = 10, graph: RGraph | None = None) → list[RArchiveRecord][source]

Return metadata for the best stored colorings.

Results are ordered by score and then coloring ID.

best_score(graph: RGraph | None = None) → int | None[source]

Return the lowest stored score.

If graph is supplied, only colorings belonging to that problem are considered.

close() → None[source]

Commit outstanding work and close the archive.

coloring_count(graph: RGraph | None = None) → int[source]

Return the number of unique stored colorings.

If graph is supplied, only colorings belonging to that problem are counted.

coloring_count_in_score_range(*, minimum_score: int | None = None, maximum_score: int | None = None, graph: RGraph | None = None) → int[source]

Count bounded records without loading their metadata.

colorings_in_score_range(*, minimum_score: int | None = None, maximum_score: int | None = None, limit: int | None = None, graph: RGraph | None = None) → list[RArchiveRecord][source]

Return records ordered by score within inclusive bounds.

load_coloring(coloring_id: int, graph: RGraph) → RArchivedColoring[source]

Restore one coloring using a compatible graph.

save_coloring(coloring: RColoring, *, run_name: str, iteration: int) → RArchiveRecord[source]

Save or observe one exact coloring.

The histogram and score are calculated from the coloring inside the archive boundary. Callers cannot accidentally supply metadata belonging to a different coloring.

If the coloring already exists, its observation count and most recent provenance are updated.

class ramsey.RSearch(environment: REnvironment, policy: RPolicy)[source]

Bases: object

Run an environment using one interchangeable policy.

RSearch coordinates an episode but does not:

  • construct seed colorings;

  • choose how action rewards are calculated;

  • implement tabu memory;

  • persist results;

  • plot results; or

  • train neural networks.

Those responsibilities belong to separate components.

Return the environment used for each search attempt.

property policy: RPolicy

Return the action-selection policy.

run(coloring: RColoring, *, record_steps: bool = False) → RSearchResult[source]

Run from an explicit seed until termination or truncation.

Parameters:

  • coloring – Immutable seed coloring for the search attempt.

  • record_steps –

    If true, preserve every RStepResult in the returned result.

    If false, only summary information and important coloring snapshots are retained.

class ramsey.RSearchState(coloring: RColoring)[source]

Bases: object

Incrementally maintained state for symmetric two-color search.

RSearchState is the sole owner of mutable coloring, clique-count, histogram, and score data.

property action_profiles: ndarray[Any, dtype[uint16]]

Return incrementally maintained all-edge clique profiles.

profiles[e, k] is the number of indexed cliques containing edge e that currently contain exactly k color-one edges.

The profiles are constructed only on first use. Once they exist, every edge flip updates only the profile contributions of cliques affected by that flip.

apply_edge_flip(edge: int) → int[source]

Flip one edge and return the exact score reduction.

A positive result means the score improved. A negative result means the score became worse.

apply_edge_recoloring(edges: ndarray[Any, dtype[integer]], colors: ndarray[Any, dtype[integer]]) → int[source]

Recolor several distinct edges and return exact score reduction.

Only edges whose requested color differs from the current color are mutated.

Each changed edge goes through apply_edge_flip(), preserving all incrementally maintained state:

  • edge colors

  • K5 color counts

  • histogram

  • monochromatic score

  • action-profile cache

  • state version

property clique_size: int

Return the forbidden clique size maintained by this state.

Return a read-only view of per-clique color-one counts.
